results: The actual analytic-order count has finite support on the entire unbounded corrected tail strip: physical spectral discreteness and the proved root localization place its support in a bounded actual physical spectral set.

The verified generic analytic zero-multiset theorem constructs two actual singular endpoint roots with their exact repetitions. Native spectral reality and sorting give an intrinsic ordered real pair; both endpoints are actual eigenvalues with nonzero vectors in the entire original H1 domain.

Each actual pair exhausts the full corrected closed strip, with actual original physical algebraic multiplicity equal to Multiset{left,right}.count at every strip point. The ordered pair is unique independently of its construction.
Distinct endpoints have actual algebraic multiplicity1, and a collapsed pair has actual multiplicity2. Native real semisimplicity gives the same geometric dimensions in the unchanged H1 domain.

Actual pair endpoints lie within sqrt(n)/4 of pi^2*n^2. Their gap is nonnegative and at most sqrt(n)/2, and their midpoint lies within sqrt(n)/4. The actual pairs are strictly separated across distinct high mode numbers, also for different potentials whenever both pairs have been constructed.

The full-strip actual coupling radius has explicit bound2*(1+2n)^r*norm(q), reusing one common pointwise coupling-product bound. The actual physical gap obeys the source square-root-six coupling estimate, hence the doubled-frequency normalized bound2*sqrt6*norm(q) and ordinary mode-number weighted bound6*sqrt6*norm(q).

Original physical source wrappers retain the complete original potential distribution, exact original norm, real mean-zero period-one constraints and full original H1 eigenvectors. One cutoff chosen before the potential on each original norm ball constructs an actual ordered high-pair family.

The actual high-gap sequence, evenly extended to signed indices and explicitly zero below the cutoff, belongs to WeightedCoeff(Weight.sobolev(-r),infinity) with its true infinity-exponent norm at most6*sqrt6*norm(q). A single original norm-ball cutoff gives the ordered family and this weighted sequence, without a finite-p substitute.
